content.text:
It throttles by default. In the installed `agents` package, `useAgentChat` groups chat state updates into a 50 ms window before re-rendering, so a fast burst of streamed chunks doesn't cause one render per chunk. The first chunk always renders right away (`node_modules/agents/dist/chat/react.d.ts:251-260`).

You can change this with the `throttle` option. Pass a number of milliseconds for a different window, or `throttle: false` to render every chunk as it arrives. `0` also turns throttling off. The older `experimental_throttle` name still works but is deprecated.

The hook passes the value to the AI SDK's `useChat` under both option names (`node_modules/agents/dist/chat/react.js:14-36`), so it works with AI SDK v3 and v4.
